query: The Landlady's Offer After closing, the landlady counts the till, then counts you in. She wants to keep you on after graduation, full time, behind the bar and, in a year or two, in charge of it. "You remember who ordered the spiced cider," she says. "That's rarer than magic." Answer by the last day. Shake on it, in principle You shake on it over the bar. She pours you a cider on the house, which has never happened to anyone before. Ask about the card games upstairs "You'd look the other way," she says, "and so would I." The offer stands. So does the question of what you'd be looking away from.

Behind the Bar
The landlady sets the cellar key on the bar between you. "You pour from tonight," she says. "Barkeeps feed the fire, too. It hasn't gone out in my lifetime, nor my mother's. Don't be the one." The hearth crackles, as if listening.
